tips.text: Keep your basics for these subjects crystal clear. Start preparing for core subjects and aptitude 3-4 months before the season starts.
Revision is the key here. I had made notes in my 2nd year about those subjects. Also I had made formula sheets about Aptitude which helped. So I just revised these things and went for the OA.
One important thing I noticed is that the questions were not section-wise so be prepared to see an aptitude question just after an oops question.
Please focus on speaking and articulating your thoughts well. Try to think how you will structure your answer in the given 30 seconds.
Do not make any scripts, or use GPT in any form for making these answers, because that will completely look unnatural.

I think they did observe the body language and eye contact with the camera. So try to maintain a good posture, hand movements and good eye contact with the camera. Keep a decent smile (don’t overdo) on your face while speaking the answers. Visualize as if you are speaking to a real person, it helps.

Know your Resume INSIDE OUT: Make sure you have at least some idea about each and every word written on your resume. Please don’t write anything that you have no idea about, it will create a very bad impression

DSA is Important: Though I was not asked about complex DSA, it is always good to be prepared about anything and everything. I started my DSA (leetcode) prep after my 2nd year ended, and I followed Striver’s A2Z DSA course for it. Though it prepared me for all sorts of patterns and topics, I still lacked the intuition. I can solve questions when they are related to some patterns, but it takes a fairly large amount of time to decode the problem when it is something completely new. Therefore, I feel you should have both Intuition and Pattern recognition. I will suggest starting with Leetcode daily questions to build your intuition starting from your 3rd sem. Gradually from there, transition into topics and their questions and then start with the sheet. This will make sure you have both the Intuition and Pattern Recognition.
Internship experience adds value: My interview had good questions about my internship. It’s important to clearly explain what you worked on, what you learnt and what impact you had.

Build Projects that have some value: Do not build generic projects, try to see what real-world problems can you solve and try to solve that in your projects. It may not be perfect, but is still way better than something too generic.

Communication is super important: See I have some friends who have a great technical profile but are rejected because of their soft skills. You may be a genius, but if you can’t make the world aware about it, then what’s the point? Hence try to focus on being vocal about your thought process, maintain good eye contact, a sincere smile, practice articulating your thoughts well, don’t speak too fast or too slow or too vague. Take pauses wherever required, try to structure your answers. THAT’S IT, there’s no Rocket Science in it! If possible and time permits, try to do a couple of mock Interviews, it will greatly help.

Consistency and Discipline over EVERYTHING: Whatever you do, stay consistent with it. I remember, when starting out, I used to get anxious when I couldn’t solve a problem, but with time and effort, I did manage to solve those.

Sometimes, it’s not your fault: See, you are about to have a completely new experience in your life. There will be times when things will just not work out, no matter how much effort you put in, something undesirable will happen. It is 60% skills and 40% LUCK according to me! I lost opportunities in MSCI, UBS because the test platform had some issues. I lost Barclays. I lost IDFC First Bank because I was asked something that was not in my knowledge and I got anxious answering that (that’s a different story altogether haha) Then I had prepared for Hyperverge so well, I spent almost 2-2.5 days, still was not shortlisted. It is what it is! These are the times you should stay calm, trust your efforts, spend time with your loved ones, trust whichever god you believe in. Don’t take too much stress, don’t let it take a toll on your health.

tips.text: I suggest preparing for CS fundamentals a month prior to placements and having handy notes to revise whenever required. It may get exhausting studying the same concepts over and over again but trust me it’s worth it.
Time management is key here, dont be stuck on any question for too long.

I suggest being as natural as possible throughout the interview and staying confident. It is okay if you fumble a little — just be confident enough to recover from it and don’t let it affect your overall presence.
Wear formal attire.
Sit in a quiet, secluded room with no disturbances.
Use headphones to ensure good sound quality.

My suggestion here would be to mention things you are very confident about, as the first few questions are usually follow-ups to your introduction. You are the one who decides the flow of the interview so answer thoughtfully and only discuss topics you know inside out.
My biggest advice here is to carefully understand the question and, if possible, relate it to a past experience.
The key is to stay calm and confident, and most importantly, be yourself. They are not looking for textbook answers; they want authentic, personal responses. So be honest and answer with confidence.

Firstly, placements are a lengthy process, and a lot of it is luck-based, so don’t lose hope and always keep pushing for the next opportunity. There will be one company where your skills match, and your luck will shine as well, so always be at your A-game and don’t miss any opportunities. Don't be disheartened by rejections, there are better opportunities waiting for you.

KNOW YOUR RESUME INSIDE OUT – I cannot stress this enough. It is absolutely crucial to know every single word you have mentioned on your resume. Please do not lie on it—having a smaller set of skills that you know thoroughly is far better than listing 20 skills that you only know at a surface level.
Also, be thorough with your projects: understand how they work, the challenges you faced, and why you chose that particular tech stack.

Find a DSA sheet that works for you and just start with it—don’t spend too much time looking for the “right material,” because there isn’t one. Just pick something and start solving it consistently. I started focusing dedicatedly on DSA in sem 6, and that was quite late, to be honest, so I suggest starting a little earlier.
Solve aptitude questions from indiabix.
Understand and practice OOPS questions and its applications since it’s a very commonly asked topic.
Understand topics well enough that you can teach them to anyone. Use active recall since that really helped me.
Try to maintain a good CGPA (preferably above 8. But a minimum of 7.5) mine was 7.77 and I did regret not having a better CGPA.
If you’re from EXTC, there are already a few companies you won’t be eligible for, so be prepared for that and don’t get discouraged too quickly.

tips.text: Don’t do this, always keep your answer to the point and crisp.
if you’re unsure, be upfront so the interviewer can move on to areas you’re confident in.
keep your attitude professional and avoid interrupting others.
Always revise core topics at least a day before the interview.
Time management is key so attempt confident questions first, then move to elimination or educated guesses.
make sure to cover these areas as well.
don’t lose hope until results are declared ;)
Try to include as many keywords of the company's values as possible.
give answers from personal experiences.
Don’t try to read it from script, speak naturally.
if you live in a PG, inform your roommates beforehand and handle distractions like the doorbell early on.
choose the quietest spot possible and keep your phone on silent.
Remember guys your introduction decides the flow for the rest of the interview, it should include your name, branch, proficiency in which languages, and your interest.
Including unique projects on your resume helps divert their attention there more, so try building such projects.
know the in and out about everything mentioned in your resume, even though it’s a group project, it's important to know the entire flow of the project.
Remember transparency and reliable product delivery are the core company values so answer these questions in that regard.
For OA practice Aptitude from IndiaBix

CCN, DBMS refer to GFG.
For Digital Interview, practice answering in front of a mirror or with a friend to build confidence and get a second perspective.
For tech rounds, be thorough with your resume, know answers to questions like why, how and what for all your projects.
Keep answers ready for questions related to the choice of your tech stack and implementation, challenges and if you were to scale this project further what would you do?
remember only to use those technological terms while answering that you are sure about, if you say OCR be prepared for questions related to it.
be prepared for it as well as schema design related questions.
For the HR round, familiarize yourself with standard questions.
Maintain good body language and develop communication skills as it really affects the entire interview process.
Research about the company well beforehand, this will show your eagerness to join.
Don’t allow awkward silence ever, keep the interview as engaging as possible.
Don’t get demotivated by rejections, it’s okay to be sad for that day, but you gotta pick yourself up and prepare for the next companies.
Try to not be that hard on yourself and take short breaks in between to avoid burn outs.
Know what works for you and maintain your physical as well as mental health.
do your best and leave the rest to God.
